pages.text: The yellow bus had brought them home from their vacation adventure, but Azi's backpack felt heavier than usual. Pandies drove with his slow, careful wisdom, occasionally glancing in the rearview mirror at Azi clutching something special.

"Are you ready to introduce Leon Jones to everyone?" Mama asked as they pulled into the driveway of The Westfield. Azi looked down at the white and brown stuffed puppy in his arms—the vacation find that had somehow felt like destiny when he spotted it in the little gift shop.

Leon Jones had soft floppy ears and kind button eyes that seemed to understand things. "What if they don't like having someone new?" Azi whispered to Citie, who rode quietly beside him. "What if Leon Jones doesn't fit in?"
The house looked exactly the same—green clapboard with the red door, garden growing tall in the backyard—but everything felt different knowing their circle was about to grow.
"Whisker-wiggle roll call!" Azi called from the playroom, but his voice was uncertain. His usual companions sat in their familiar spots on the circular rug, while Leon Jones waited in Azi's lap.

Jujy puffed up his black-and-white chest. "I'm Jujy, the confident leader, and I—" He paused, noticing the newcomer. "Who's that?" "This is Leon Jones," Azi said carefully. "He... he wanted to come home with us."
Dory tilted her gray-and-white head with dreamy curiosity. "Does he have a job like the rest of us? I'm the dreamy scout, Pandies drives the bus, Monkie knows about fishing..."
Leon Jones just sat quietly, his button eyes taking everything in. "What if he doesn't need a job?" Azi asked. "What if he's just... Leon Jones?"

The first few days felt different. During AKAI keyboard time, Leon Jones sat beside Azi while he played his three-chord progression. The stuffed puppy seemed to listen carefully, as if learning the rhythm of their household.

When Clappy started his joyful clapping, Leon Jones didn't join in, but he didn't seem startled either. He just watched with patient button eyes. "He's very quiet," observed Slothie in his slow, thoughtful way. "Some friends speak with their presence."

Azi found himself carrying Leon Jones everywhere—to puzzle time, to garden walks, to evening moon-watching by the window. But something felt incomplete. Leon Jones was with them, but not quite part of them yet.
"Maybe," Azi said to Monkie during one of their imaginary fishing trips, "making friends takes time, even with stuffed animals."

It happened during a trampoline afternoon in the backyard. Azi was bouncing with his usual companions when Leon Jones tumbled from his arms and landed in the garden bed near the tomatoes. "Oh no!" Azi called, stopping his bouncing. "Leon Jones!"

But as Azi climbed down to rescue him, he noticed something. Leon Jones had landed right next to a small tomato plant that was drooping in the heat. His soft body was providing just enough shade to keep the little plant cool.
"Look," whispered Dory. "He's helping." "Without even trying," added Jujy, his usual confidence tempered with something like respect. Azi gently picked up Leon Jones, brushing off a few leaves.
"Maybe that's what you do," he said softly. "Maybe you help just by being exactly where you need to be."
After that, everything changed. Leon Jones found his place not through announcing it like Jujy, or dreaming it like Dory, but by simply belonging.

During roll call, he became the quiet listener—the one who made space for everyone else's voices. When Clappy got too excited, Leon Jones's calm presence helped settle the energy. When puzzle pieces scattered, he was the soft landing that kept them from rolling away.
"You know what?" Azi said one evening as they all gathered for moon-watching. "Leon Jones doesn't need a job title. He just needs to be Leon Jones."
Pandies nodded his slow approval. "Some wisdom," he said carefully, "lives in simply being present."

"Whisker-wiggle roll call!" Azi called from the playroom, and now Leon Jones was part of the rhythm. He didn't announce himself with words, but his quiet presence filled a space no one had realized was empty.
"I'm Jujy, the confident leader!" "I'm Dory, the dreamy scout!" "I'm Pandies, the wise guide!" "I'm Citie, the steady observer!"
"I'm Clappy, the joyful musician!" "I'm Monkie, the practical fisherman!" "I'm Peter, the quiet trickster!" "I'm Slothie, and this is Baby Slothie!"
And Leon Jones, who simply wagged his stuffed tail in response. "Welcome home, Leon Jones," Azi said, settling onto the circular rug with all his friends. "Welcome to our circle."

Outside, the moon watched over The Westfield, over all the children learning that sometimes the best friends are the ones who love you just by being themselves, and sometimes the most important gift you can give is making room for someone new.
Azi strummed his guitar softly, playing a melody that now included everyone—a song about vacation discoveries and coming home, about circles that grow to include whoever needs to belong.

when you are not quite sure about something yet
able to wait calmly, without fussing or hurrying
bending over and sagging down, the way a flower does when it is thirsty
spread out all over the place, every which way
to get calm and quiet again after being excited
the feeling that someone is right there with you, even when they are quiet
the part of a song you can hum
